newsitem.title: FRANCE: Skilled negotiator Le Pensec named farm minister.
newsitem.headline: Skilled negotiator Le Pensec named farm minister.

text.p: Louis Le Pensec, a skilled negotiator and former minister of the sea, was named on Wednesday as France's farm and fisheries minister in the Socialist-led government of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
A former social sciences teacher at Rennes university, the discreet but efficient Le Pensec has also held office as a Socialist government spokesman and overseas territories minister.
His negotiating skills will be sorely tested in dealing with France's restive farmers, who are angry over cheap imports from south European countries and traditionally hostile to the Socialists.

Le Pensec, 60, was minister of the sea from 1981 to 1983 and again briefly in 1988. He led the regional coastal nature preservation body from 1983 to 1985, an experience that should prove useful as farm and fisheries minister.

As minister for overseas territories from 1988 to 1993, he shared credit for a 1988 accord that ended bloodshed between Europeans and Melanesian separatists in New Caledonia, a French territory in the South Pacific.
The accord, following violence in which 19 pro-independence activists and three gendarmes were killed, included the promise of an referendum on independence to be held in 1998.
Le Pensec, mayor since 1971 of his native village of Mellac in Brittany in northwest France, was re-elected to the National Assembly on June 1, polling 59 percent of the votes on the runoff round.
A deputy of Concarneau since 1973, he had successfully survived a Socialist party rout in the parliamentary electons of 1993.
Born in 1937 in a working-class family of eight, Le Pensec studied political science and sociology in Rennes and in Paris.
He worked for French aero engine company Snecma in the mid-1960s and for Saviem, a former unit of French carmaker Renault, in the 1970s.
He taught social sciences at the University of Rennes before entering parliament. He is married with one child.
